title: The Fence Principle
equation: Removal Safety = Understanding of Its Original Purpose (rate 1-10)
hook: That annoying rule nobody can explain probably exists for a reason.
statement: Don't get rid of a rule until you understand why it was put there.
explainer: Most rules once solved a real problem you might not see anymore. Deleting one you don't understand isn't bold. It's betting the old danger is gone.
sop: Pick the rule or process you want to cut.
Find out who added it and what problem it solved. Ask, don't guess.
Rate your Understanding of Its Original Purpose from 1 to 10.
If it's low, keep the rule and keep digging.
Remove it only once you know the original risk is gone.
equation_example: You rate your understanding of why the rule exists at 3 out of 10. 3 ÷ 10 = 0.3, so leave it alone for now. Get that to 9 ÷ 10 = 0.9 and you can cut it with real confidence.
question: Name one rule you want to delete and write down why it was created.
closing_statement: Know why it's there before you tear it down.
caption:
